It formally states that for independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) random variables with mean μ and variance σ², the distribution of their standardized sum converges to the standard normal distribution as the sample size n approaches infinity. The text highlights the CLT's utility in approximating probabilities involving sums of i.i.d. variables and notes the use of the ±0.5 continuity correction when dealing with discrete distributions.
